subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Is exact consent to the displayed `claws add` plan sufficient authorization to install a process-wide plugin, or must shared-plugin mutation require a separate host-level grant?
rationale: The implementation intentionally makes plugins shared-host resources, so this choice sets the authority boundary for sibling agents and ordinary OpenClaw operations rather than resolving a mechanical defect.

options.title: Require an explicit host-level grant
options.body: Keep skill installation as proposed, but require a separately visible host-level acknowledgement before a Claw plan can install or mutate a shared plugin.

options.title: Accept exact-plan consent
options.body: Approve the current model in which the displayed exact plan is the host authorization for the shared plugin action.

options.title: Defer shared plugins
options.body: Land only the workspace-scoped skill path and keep shared-plugin package actions blocked until the host authorization model is settled.

recommendation.title: Require an explicit host-level grant
recommendation.body: Keep skill installation as proposed, but require a separately visible host-level acknowledgement before a Claw plan can install or mutate a shared plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: Their package-lifecycle review established the consent, provenance, and removal requirements now at issue.
